paper.title: MatterSim: A Deep Learning Atomistic Model Across Elements, Temperatures and Pressures

result.summary: MatterSim 是一个基于深度图神经网络、主动学习和大规模第一性原理计算训练的原子尺度模型，旨在在元素、温度和压力维度上实现广泛的材料性质预测 [S1.p3][S3.p1]。它作为零样本机器学习力场，在覆盖 0–5000 K 和 0–1000 GPa 的 MPF-TP 数据集上达到 36 meV/atom 的 MAE，相比此前最优模型精度提升约十倍 [S1.p3][S2.SS1.p2]。模型还能预测声子、力学性质、自由能和相图，与第一性原理及实验相比具有接近第一性原理的精度 [S2.SS2.p3][S2.SS2.p4][S2.SS2.p5]。此外，MatterSim 可作为持续学习和定制化平台，通过微调以少量数据适配特定理论水平或直接性质预测任务 [S2.SS4.p2][S2.SS5.p2]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：现有材料数据库和模型主要基于近平衡晶体结构，而材料性质还依赖于温度和压力等热力学条件，导致配置空间巨大、现有模型泛化能力受限 [S1.p2]。因此，需要一种能在整个周期表范围内、在有限温度和压力下准确高效预测材料性质的方法 [S1.p1][S1.p3]。

evidence.quote: However, the property of a potential candidate material not only depends on its chemical composition and corresponding near-equilibrium atomic structure, but also on thermodynamic conditions including temperature and pressure.

This results in a requirement of high predictive accuracy over an enormous configuration space well beyond the ground states or local minima of crystal structures typically captured by current databases and models, which fundamentally limits their applicability for materials design.
At the core of this paradigm shift is the ability to accurately and efficiently predict the properties of arbitrary materials under practical synthesis and working conditions.

To address this challenge, we introduce MatterSim, a deep learning model designed for emulating materials and predicting their properties under realistic thermodynamic conditions including finite temperatures and pressures, as illustrated in Fig. 1.

method.text: MatterSim 采用主动学习框架，整合深度图神经网络、材料探索器、第一性原理监督器和集成不确定性监测器 [S2.SS1.p1]。第一性原理监督器在 GGA-PBE 水平（对部分材料加 Hubbard U 修正）提供能量、力和应力标签，模型作为代理引导探索器采样高不确定性区域，形成主动学习循环 [S2.SS1.p1]。模型骨干采用 M3GNet 和 Graphormer 两种架构，其中 Graphormer 被改造以支持平移不变性、周期性边界条件和显式等变特征 [S2.SS1.p3]。

evidence.quote: MatterSim employs an active learning approach to explore the extensive materials space, integrating a deep graph neural network, a materials explorer, a first-principles supervisor, and an ensemble uncertainty monitor, see Fig. 2 (a).

Starting from an initial dataset curated from existing sources, the first-principles supervisor offers the deep learning model supervision signals relating to energies, forces, and stresses on the given structures at the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) level of theory with Hubbard U correction for select materials as specified by the Materials Project standard settings.

This trained model then functions as an effective surrogate to the first-principles method, guiding the materials explorer to gather more structures, thereby exploring the most uncertain regions of materials space to enrich the samples for model training.
In this work, we opt to use two primary architectures, M3GNet and Graphormer as the backbones for MatterSim.

In particular, we baked in several additional attributes including invariance to translation and periodic boundary conditions and explicit equivariant features to better accommodate materials-related tasks, see Section S1 for more details.

experiments.text: 训练数据集包含约 1700 万个第一性原理标注结构，覆盖 0–5000 K 和 0–1000 GPa 的温度压力范围 [S2.SS1.p2]。零样本性能在多个数据集上评估，包括 MPtrj-1k、Alexandria-1k、MPtrj-highest-stress-1k，以及新创建的 MPF-Alkali-TP、MPF-TP 和 Random-TP，后三者由第一性原理分子动力学轨迹生成，温度和压力随机采样 [S6.p1][S6.p2]。此外，在 MatBench Discovery、PhononDB、力学性质、自由能和相图等任务上进行了基准测试 [S2.SS2.p2][S2.SS2.p3][S2.SS2.p4][S2.SS2.p5]。

evidence.quote: As of the date of publication, the training dataset contains $\sim$ 17M structures labeled with first-principles computations.
As shown in Fig. 2 (b), the curated dataset is representative of materials at temperatures and pressures covering 0– $5000\text{\,}\mathrm{K}$ and 0– $1000\text{\,}\mathrm{GPa}$.
MPtrj-1k and Alexandria-1k are collected by sampling randomly one thousand materials from the MPtrj and Alexandria dataset, respectively.
The MPtrj-highest-stress-1k contains the 1,000 materials with the highest stress in magnitude computed using DFT from the MPtrj datasets.

The MPF-Alkali-TP, MPF-TP, Random-TP benchmark sets are created with increasing complexity to evaluate the models’ performance on materials under finite temperature and pressure conditions with far from equilibrium atomic positions.

The temperatures and pressures are all random sampled. For the temperature, it is uniformly sampled between 0 to 5000K. For the pressure, we used a log scale when carrying out the sampling. The pressure range is from 0 to 1000 GPa.

MatterSim shows a strong capability in predicting stability of new materials, with an F1 score of 0.83 and a mean absolute energy error of the formation energy of $25\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ benchmarked on MatBench Discovery

Fig. 4 (a) shows the benchmark results on the materials from the PhononDB, using maximum phonon frequency as an indicator, and a good agreement is achieved with a mean absolute error (MAE) of $0.87\text{\,}\mathrm{THz}$.

Fig. 4 (c) shows the parity plot of the $0\text{\,}\mathrm{K}$ -bulk modulus predicted from MatterSim and their first-principles references. A remarkable agreement is achieved with an MAE of only $2.47\text{\,}\mathrm{GPa}$.

As shown in Fig. 4 (e)-(f), and Fig. S21, MatterSim achieves a sub- $10\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ error for temperatures up to $1000\text{\,}\mathrm{K}$ when compared with QHA computations at PBE level of theory, signifying a near-first-principles predictive power.

findings.text: MatterSim 在 MPF-TP 数据集上达到 36 meV/atom 的 MAE，相比此前最优模型精度提升约十倍 [S1.p3][S2.SS1.p2]。在 MatBench Discovery 上取得 F1 分数 0.83 和 25 meV/atom 的形成能 MAE [S2.SS2.p2]。声子最大频率 MAE 为 0.87 THz，0 K 体模量 MAE 为 2.47 GPa [S2.SS2.p3][S2.SS2.p4]。自由能预测与实验相比 MAE 为 15 meV/atom，优于专门在实验数据上训练的模型 [S2.SS2.p5]。通过微调，仅用 30 个构型即可达到从头训练 900 个构型的性能，数据效率提升 30 倍 [S2.SS4.p2]。

evidence.quote: with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 36 meV/atom (43 meV/atom as chemical accuracy) on MPF-TP (a dataset covering wide ranges of materials structure sampled under finite temperature between 0-5000 K and pressures between 0–1000 GPa), marking a ten-fold increase in accuracy compared with previous efforts.

The most noticeable enhancement are observed on the benchmark datasets MPF-TP and Random-TP (sampled from high temperature and pressure), where MatterSim achieves up to 10-fold improvement compared to universal force fields trained on relaxation trajectories.

MatterSim shows a strong capability in predicting stability of new materials, with an F1 score of 0.83 and a mean absolute energy error of the formation energy of $25\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ benchmarked on MatBench Discovery

Fig. 4 (a) shows the benchmark results on the materials from the PhononDB, using maximum phonon frequency as an indicator, and a good agreement is achieved with a mean absolute error (MAE) of $0.87\text{\,}\mathrm{THz}$.

Fig. 4 (c) shows the parity plot of the $0\text{\,}\mathrm{K}$ -bulk modulus predicted from MatterSim and their first-principles references. A remarkable agreement is achieved with an MAE of only $2.47\text{\,}\mathrm{GPa}$.

More importantly, when compared with experimental measurements on over 200 materials as shown in Fig. S22, it achieves an MAE of $15\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ (see Section S11.1), lower than dedicated models directly trained on experimental data.

However, with only 30 configurations sampled from an ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) trajectory with rev-PBE0-D3 level of theory, MatterSim can be efficiently fine-tuned and the resultant model (indicated as finetune-30 model) reaches the same performance as the model trained from scratch with all 900 configurations from the AIMD trajectory (denote as scratch-900) for water structural properties (see Fig. 6 (c) and Fig. 6 (d)).

Therefore, by finetuning MatterSim, we were able to obtain the similar accuracy of the scratch-900 model on this task while using only 1/30 of the training data, which clearly underscores the effectiveness of supervised pretraining on large-scale high-fidelity first-principles data with wide coverage.

limitations.text: 作者指出，MatterSim 目前采用半局域原子相互作用描述，在长程相互作用主导的场景（如聚合物和多相体系）中表现不佳 [S3.p3]。模型仅在同质体相系统上训练，未显式包含对催化等应用至关重要的表面和界面数据 [S3.p3]。此外，模型目前仅原生支持 DFT-PBE 水平的推断，限制了其在涉及复杂相互作用（如聚合物和有机液体）系统中的应用 [S3.p3]。模型目前仅支持能量、力和应力的原生预测，纳入电荷、自旋、磁矩等更多数据模态可能进一步提升精度和适用性 [S3.p3]。

evidence.quote: From the perspective of model development, it currently utilizes a semi-local description of atomic interactions, where long-range interactions majorly leverages message passing or updates on attention weights through graph nodes.

Even though this model demonstrates superior performance compared to models that rely solely on local environments,, it doesn’t perform effectively in scenarios where long-range interactions dominate the properties, such as polymeric and heterogeneous systems.
As for data coverage, the current model is trained only on homogeneous bulk systems, without explicit inclusion of surface and interface data that are crucial for applications such as catalysis.
Additionally, the model currently only naively supports inferences with DFT-PBE level of theory, limiting its use for systems involving complex interactions, such as polymers and organic liquids.

Currently, the model only supports the native prediction of energy, forces, and stresses. Including more data modalities, such as charge, spin, magnetic moments, and even more complex electronic structure features, could further enhance the model’s accuracy and applicability.
